test_title: PYST 21: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 05 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Why do we experience muscle cramps after heavy exercise?

options.text: Due to accumulation of lactic acid
Because blood flow completely stops during exercise
Due to a decrease in body temperature

solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to accumulation of lactic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscle cramps after heavy exercise** occur primarily due to the **accumulation of lactic acid** in the muscles. Lactic acid is a by-product of anaerobic respiration, which happens when the oxygen supply to the muscles is insufficient during intense physical activities.
 
• When muscles perform strenuous exercise, they may switch to **anaerobic metabolism**, leading to the buildup of lactic acid. This causes a **drop in pH levels** in the muscle tissue, resulting in a burning sensation and cramps.
 
• **Insufficient oxygen supply:** During vigorous physical activities, muscles require more oxygen. If the supply is inadequate, the muscles rely on anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid.
 
• The accumulation of lactic acid affects the **nerve endings** in the muscles, causing discomfort and cramping sensations. This phenomenon is temporary and typically resolves once the lactic acid is flushed out of the system.
 
• Proper **hydration and stretching** before and after exercise can help reduce the risk of muscle cramps caused by lactic acid buildup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anaerobic respiration:**

 
 
• Occurs when oxygen levels are insufficient for aerobic respiration.
 
• Produces energy for muscle contraction but generates **lactic acid** as a by-product.
 
• Lactic acid buildup leads to temporary muscle fatigue and cramps.
 
 
 
• **Role of lactic acid:**
 
 
• Lactic acid is cleared from the muscles and metabolized into glucose by the **liver** through a process called the **Cori cycle**.
 
• The buildup of lactic acid can lead to a **temporary decrease in muscle efficiency**.
 
 
 
• **Preventing muscle cramps:**
 
 
• Maintain proper **hydration** during and after exercise to reduce the risk of cramps.
 
• Include **electrolytes** in your diet to ensure muscle function and avoid electrolyte imbalance.
 
• Perform **warm-up and cool-down exercises** to improve blood circulation and reduce lactic acid buildup.
 
 
 
• **Misconceptions:**
 
 
• Muscle cramps are not caused by the complete cessation of blood flow (**Statement 3 is incorrect**). Blood flow increases during exercise to supply oxygen to the muscles.
 
• Muscle cramps are not due to a decrease in body temperature (**Statement 4 is incorrect**). Body temperature typically rises during exercise.
 
• Muscles do not stop contracting during cramps (**Statement 2 is incorrect**). On the contrary, cramps are due to involuntary contractions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lactic acid threshold:** This refers to the exercise intensity at which lactic acid starts accumulating significantly in the muscles. Training at or below this threshold can improve endurance.
 
• **Electrolyte imbalance:** Lack of electrolytes like sodium, potassium, and magnesium can exacerbate muscle cramps. Proper nutrition is essential for maintaining muscle function.
 
• **Stretching and massage:** Post-exercise stretching and massage can help in dissipating lactic acid and relieving cramps.
 
• **Scientific studies:** Research has shown that lactic acid is rapidly cleared from the muscles after exercise, and cramps are generally resolved within a short duration.
